en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed to move soil and water up the steep Cordillera mountains.
Jeepney tires have deep treads to increase friction and prevent slipping when driving on wet asphalt roads in Manila during the rainy season.
Earth's gravity pulls water downward, causing the stunning Pagsanjan Falls in Laguna to continuously cascade down the rocky cliff into the river below.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos contain magnetite, a highly magnetic mineral that can be strongly attracted to a permanent magnet.
The Makiling-Banahaw geothermal power plant in Laguna converts underground heat energy from volcanoes into electricity to power local homes.
The fine white coral sand of Boracay reflects most sunlight, making the beach look bright and feel cooler to bare feet.
Visitors in the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River hear loud echoes because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone walls of the cave.
A traditional clay palayok conducts heat slowly and evenly from the charcoal fire, making it perfect for simmering Filipino chicken tinola.
Carabaos get kinetic energy to plow rice fields by digesting grass, converting the stored chemical energy in the plant into movement.
The large wooden wheels of a traditional horse-drawn calesa in Vigan act as wheel and axle simple machines to roll smoothly.
In a bamboo steamer used for making siopao, hot steam rises through the layers to cook the buns using convection.
Rubbing a dried tamarind seed pod against a cotton shirt generates static electricity that can attract small pieces of paper.
